about.title: Temecula Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Eight people died on Temecula roads in 2025, according to public collision records for the most recent final year in this part of Riverside County. Behind each of those counts is a household that now has to figure out what comes next. A wrongful death claim is one part of that, and it is a civil matter, entirely separate from any criminal charges a driver may face. In California, the right to bring the claim belongs first to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and the children; when there are none, certain dependents and heirs may step in. The claim can seek funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and shorter when a public agency is involved, which can matter on stretches like I-15 or Rancho California Road. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Temecula families with an independent attorney who takes these cases on contingency.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can tell you early whether you have the right to bring the claim and how relatives coordinate.

items.title: Deadlines tracked from day one
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, but a claim involving a city, county or Caltrans has a much shorter window. The attorney you are connected with will map those dates right away.

items.title: Free to connect, contingency to hire
items.desc: LawProactive charges nothing to match you with an independent attorney, and that attorney works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: The crash happened on I-15 in Temecula. Does the highway change my claim?
items.answer: It can. Freeways in the Temecula area are maintained by Caltrans, and if road design or maintenance played any role, a government claim with a much shorter deadline than two years may apply. An attorney can look at the collision report and decide whether a public entity needs to be put on notice quickly.

items.question: The driver is being prosecuted. Do we have to wait for the criminal case?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves on its own track, regardless of whether the Riverside County District Attorney files charges or wins a conviction. Evidence from the criminal case can sometimes help, but your family does not have to wait for it to finish before acting.

items.question: What can our family actually recover?
items.answer: California allows recovery of funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided over their expected lifetime, and the loss of their love, companionship, guidance and care. Each family's losses look different, and no attorney can promise a particular result. What they can do is document those losses carefully so nothing is left out.
